chunk_findings.detail: The new `sweep_interval_s` knob defaults to 900 seconds, but the old behavior—stated in the knob’s own doc as “0 sweeps on every brief, as before”—was to run `dispose_finished` on every `brief`. On an upgraded repo with finished leftover worktrees and no `.ddflow/local/sweep-finished.last`, `ddflow brief` will now skip the sweep for up to 15 minutes instead of sweeping immediately. This violates [r-everything-configurable], which requires a new knob to default to the old behavior; the default should be 0 (with cadence opt-in).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/worktree.py:sweep_interval_s

chunk_findings.detail: `prefetch_on_base` runs `git rev-list --no-walk <chunk> ^<base> --` and treats every printed object id as “base lacks this commit.” But `--no-walk` deliberately does not traverse ancestors of a negative revision: if `<A>` is an ancestor of `<base>`, `git rev-list --no-walk <A> ^<base>` still prints `<A>`. So a worktree whose HEAD is `<A>`, already reachable from the base, leads `prefetch_on_base(["<A>"], "<base>")` to cache `_on_base[(<A>, <base>)]` as `False`, and a later `on_base("<A>", "<base>")` returns `False` when the true answer is `True` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <A> <base>` exits 0). The code comment’s claim that this prints “exactly the listed commits the base lacks” is false, and the wrong reachability answer can drive an incorrect finished/sweep classification.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/gitbatch.py: RepoFacts.prefetch_on_base

chunk_findings.detail: With the new default `lease.scan_view_trees_max = 16` and the stated 126 stale leases in the falsifier, `_measure` will measure 16 worktrees. For each measured tree it calls `W.tree_work(wt, base, ahead=False)` for dirty files and then `facts.ahead(wt, base)` for the ahead count. Those are two git subprocesses per measured tree, so just these calls produce 32 subprocesses before the initial `RepoFacts` queries. That makes the change's own falsifier "more than 30 git subprocesses for status with 126 stale leases" true, not false.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/recovery.py:_measure

chunk_findings.detail: The note records `new = "16"`. The pre-change `_measure` this diff replaces had no cap: status/brief measured every stale worktree. A repository with 17 stale worktrees therefore changes from measuring all 17 to measuring 16 and marking the 17th as NOT MEASURED. That is not the old behaviour, contradicting the change's CONFORMANCE claim that "a new knob defaults to the old behaviour"; it is a semantic behaviour change for existing users, not merely additive.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.lease.scan_view_trees_max.toml:new

chunk_findings.detail: The submitted CONFORMANCE clause states “a new knob defaults to the old behaviour”, but neither new knob in this part does: `worktree.sweep_interval_s` defaults to `900`, while the old behavior was a sweep on every `brief` (only `0` restores that behavior), and `lease.scan_view_verdicts_max` defaults to `0`, while the old status/brief behavior was to weigh all such items (only a value above 0 restores that path). A repository upgraded with no config changes therefore gets the new behavior immediately: finished worktrees are not swept for up to 15 minutes, and status/brief no longer do the old full scan. This contradicts the stated [r-upgrade-safe] default-compatibility criterion.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.worktree.sweep_interval_s.toml:6 and ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.lease.scan_view_verdicts_max.toml:6

chunk_findings.detail: The test hard-codes the default read-only view cap as 16: `assert sum(1 for r in capped if r.salvageable is None) == 20 - 16`. Since `view=True` is the read-only path used by `RP.status`, a default `status` on the stated 126-stale-lease scenario will measure only 16 leases and leave 110 as “NOT MEASURED”. That conflicts with the CONFORMANCE requirement that the new `lease.scan_view_trees_max` knob defaults to the old behaviour; old `status` measured every expired lease, so the default must be uncapped. Either conforming code fails this assertion, or the shipped default violates the requirement.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_git_batch.py::test_recover_still_measures_every_tree

chunk_findings.detail: This test calls `LC.brief` twice without setting `worktree.sweep_interval_s`, then asserts only one `sweep_finished` call. But the CONFORMANCE requirement says the new `worktree.sweep_interval_s` knob defaults to the old behaviour, where `brief` ran `sweep_finished` on every invocation; that default must therefore be `0`, and with `0` each of the two calls in this test invokes the patched `sweep_finished`, making `len(calls) == 2` and failing the assertion. If the default is positive to make this test pass, the build violates the stated conformance.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_git_batch.py::test_brief_sweeps_finished_worktrees_at_most_once_per_interval

chunk_findings.detail: The new `sweep_interval_s` knob defaults to `900`, but its own doc says `0` is the old behaviour (“0 sweeps on every brief, as before”), and the change’s CONFORMANCE clause claims “a new knob defaults to the old behaviour.” Concrete failure: on an existing project after upgrading with no config change, `ddflow brief` no longer sweeps finished worktrees on every call. Run `brief`, finish a worktree, run `brief` again within 900 seconds; the second run skips the sweep it would have performed before this change, leaving the leftover worktree until the interval elapses. The default should be `0` to preserve old behaviour, or the conformance claim is false.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/worktree.py:sweep_interval_s

chunk_findings.detail: `on_base` collapses an unknown result into `False`. When `git merge-base --is-ancestor sha base` exits 128 (for example `sha` is an unknown object or not a commit), `on_base` returns `False`, which means "sha is not on base". That contradicts the module docstring's stated contract "An answer git could not give is ``None`` / -1, never a guess: unknown is not zero." A caller that uses `False` to decide whether scanning is unnecessary will act as though the commit is absent rather than unavailable, and the unknown key is not cached, so repeated unknown queries respawn subprocesses too.
chunk_findings.title: RepoFacts.on_base

chunk_findings.detail: The new port-like git/file-system accesses import `git` and `worktree` from `ddflow.infra` (`from . import git as G`, `from . import worktree as W`), but the project rule [r-adapters] requires every external dependency (git, filesystem layout, subprocess tools, etc.) to go through a port in `ddflow/adapters`. This change assumes `infra.git` satisfies `r-adapters`; as written it is outside `ddflow/adapters` and should use the adapter port instead.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/gitbatch.py:5-6

chunk_findings.detail: `gather` and `inspect` declare `view: bool = False` and `_expired` forwards that value to `L.scan(..., view=view)`. In this same change `L.scan`'s `view` is not a boolean switch: it is the precomputed `gitbatch.RepoFacts` batching object added in `ddflow/infra/gitbatch.py` (the object governed by the new `lease.scan_view_trees_max`/`lease.scan_view_verdicts_max` limits). Any call that uses the fallback path (`recoveries=None`)—for example an existing call `healthwatch.gather(log, st, cfg, repo, now)`—passes `False` as `L.scan`'s `view`. Because `False` is not `None`, `L.scan` will treat `False` as an already-built `RepoFacts` object and then access its tree/verdict fields on a bool, raising `AttributeError`/`TypeError`. This breaks every legacy call site that has not yet been changed to pass `recoveries`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/healthwatch.py:151 (_expired/gather/_inspect)

chunk_findings.detail: The diff changes both `_measure` and `_note_landed` calls to pass extra positional arguments (`facts` and `budget`) — e.g. `_measure(rec, repo, cfg, facts, budget)` — but this part contains no corresponding update to the definitions of `_measure`/`_note_landed`; they retain their previous signatures (`_measure(rec, repo, cfg)` and `_note_landed(rec, it, state, cfg, repo)`). Any state that reaches the active-lease `else` branch or the leftover-worktree branch will immediately raise `TypeError` (`_measure() takes 3 positional arguments but 5 were given`), so `status`, `brief`, `recover`, and `sweep` crash on the first expired lease or leftover tree instead of returning recoveries.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/recovery.py:98,119 (`scan_recovery` call sites)

chunk_findings.detail: The new knob `lease.scan_view_trees_max` defaults to `"16"` and `_measure` now skips measurement once that budget is exhausted, marking further stale worktrees `salvageable = None` / “NOT MEASURED”. Pre-change `_measure` had no such cap and measured every stale worktree, so the default does **not** preserve the old behaviour. Given a repo with 17 stale clean worktrees, status/brief will no longer measure the 17th and will treat it as holding work; this contradicts the stated conformance requirement that a new knob default to the old behaviour.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.lease.scan_view_trees_max.toml:new

chunk_findings.detail: `impact = "additive"` is wrong because the new default `worktree.sweep_interval_s = 900` changes existing `brief` behavior: before, `brief` swept finished worktrees on every call; with the default it suppresses a sweep if one occurred within the previous 900 seconds. A user running `brief` every five minutes will now accumulate finished worktrees without changing any config, yet the upgrade note classifies this as additive rather than a behavior change.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.worktree.sweep_interval_s.toml:7

chunk_findings.detail: `impact = "additive"` is wrong because `new = "0"` disables the previous default status/brief full verdict scan. The note’s own `why` text says status and brief “no longer weigh the full completion” and user action (`set above 0`) is required to restore any of it, so this is a user-visible behavior change on upgrade, not merely an additive knob.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.lease.scan_view_verdicts_max.toml:7

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert len(calls) == 1` only passes if the new `worktree.sweep_interval_s` default is positive, so two consecutive `brief` calls on an unconfigured repo sweep once. The change’s own CONFORMANCE text requires “a new knob defaults to the old behaviour” [r-upgrade-safe]; old `brief` called `sweep_finished` on every invocation. With the default this test requires, two back-to-back `brief` runs on a new repo sweep once instead of twice, violating that upgrade-safety requirement.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_git_batch.py:test_brief_sweeps_finished_worktrees_at_most_once_per_interval

chunk_findings.detail: The new guard `return now - float(_sweep_stamp_path(repo).read_text().strip()) >= every` only catches `OSError`/`ValueError`, but a corrupt stamp containing `"nan"` parses successfully without raising. `float("nan")` produces NaN, so `now - NaN >= every` is always `False`, making `_sweep_due` return `False` on every call and permanently preventing `CL.sweep_finished` from running for that repo. The previous code did not return `False` in that case; it would overwrite the corrupt stamp and perform the sweep. Concrete input: `.ddflow/local/sweep-finished.last` contains `nan\n`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py:_sweep_due

chunk_findings.detail: `RepoFacts.on_base` checks `r.code not in (0, 1)` and then returns `False` on line 128 when the code is outside `(0, 1)`. But line 130 returns `r.ok` (which means `r.code == 0`), meaning that any non-zero exit code except those not in `(0, 1)` falls through to line 130 where `r.ok` is `False`, which correctly returns `False`. However, when `r.code` is something like 128 (unknown commit), line 128 returns `False` and caches `self._on_base[key] = False`, treating an unknown commit as "not an ancestor" rather than an error or unknown state, contradicting the docstring comment which says "unknown: not remembered".
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/gitbatch.py:127
